description: December 9 birthday meaning: Sagittarius decan 2, birthday number 9, Life Path by year, Chinese zodiac note and famous birthdays.
answer: In Western astrology, a December 9 birthday falls in Sagittarius, in the second decan, with Jupiter as the sign's ruler and Mars as the decan's. In numerology the day gives birthday number 9. The Life Path also uses the birth year. Sagittarius is mutable and fire.

sections.heading: December 9 zodiac sign and personality
paragraphs: Seventeen degrees of Sagittarius and the birthday number 9 give December 9 a crusading flavour. Mars, sub-ruler of this decan, supplies courage, while 9 is linked with compassion and the bigger picture. Traditionally, that adds up to an idealist willing to act: someone who joins the campaign, carries the banner and argues passionately for fairness.

On December 9 the Sun usually sits at about 17° Sagittarius, in the second decan, where Mars is the sub-ruler alongside Jupiter. Mars, ruler of Aries, acts as sub-ruler for the middle of Sagittarius, roughly December 2 to December 11. The sign's love of freedom picks up a sharper, more competitive edge. Early-December birthdays are frequently linked with bold, energetic people who are quick to champion a cause, whether on a playing field, in a debate or on the road. Their honesty may be direct enough to startle. Mars brings drive and courage, along with impatience when life moves slowly. Channelled well, this mix of vision and nerve makes for a natural pioneer, someone willing to test an idea in the real world.

sections.heading: December 9 in numerology
paragraphs: Born on the 9th, your birthday number is 9, the last and broadest of the single digits. Numerologists see the birth day as a secondary number that describes a natural gift. The 9 is traditionally associated with compassion, idealism and a wide view of humanity, perhaps because it contains something of every number before it. Those with this birthday often find themselves helping, teaching or creating for audiences beyond their own circle. Letting go can be a recurring theme for 9s, along with learning that finishing one chapter makes space for a better one.

The Life Path, the main number in a numerology chart, also uses the birth year, so it changes from one December 9 birthday to the next: it is 1 for 1960, 2 for 1970, 3 for 1980 and 4 for 1990, for example.

sections.heading: Born on December 9: season, famous birthdays and Chinese zodiac
paragraphs: December birthdays arrive at the start of northern winter, around the shortest days and the year's festivities, and at the start of summer in the southern hemisphere. Sagittarius holds most of the month, with Capricorn beginning around December 21 or 22. In numerology December is month 12, which reduces to 3: expression and sociability, built from the 1 and 2 of initiative and partnership. December 9 is the 343rd day of the year (344th in a leap year). By December 22, 13 days later, the Sun has usually moved on into Capricorn.

For the Chinese zodiac, Lunar New Year has always passed by December 9, so the animal is simply the one for the birth year. Well-known people born on December 9 include Peter Kropotkin (1842), Kirk Douglas (1916) and Jean-Claude Juncker (1954).

faq.question: What zodiac sign is December 9?
faq.answer: December 9 is Sagittarius in every year from 1930 to 2030, wherever you were born. It falls in the second decan of Sagittarius, which tradition links with Mars.

faq.question: What is the Life Path number for someone born on December 9?
faq.answer: It depends on the birth year. On December 9 the Life Path is 1 in 1960, 2 in 1970, 3 in 1980, 4 in 1990, 5 in 2000, 6 in 2010 and 7 in 2020. The birthday number, from the day alone, is 9 for everyone born on the 9th.

faq.question: What Chinese zodiac sign is someone born on December 9?
faq.answer: Chinese astrology is straightforward for a December 9 birthday: the new year began weeks earlier, so the birth year's own animal applies.

faq.question: Which famous people were born on December 9?
faq.answer: December 9 is also the birthday of Peter Kropotkin (1842), Kirk Douglas (1916) and Jean-Claude Juncker (1954). The list comes from Wikidata and favours people with the most Wikipedia articles.
